findings.finding: Kei raises how to convey feedback. Sensei's written choice group articulates the danger of replacing the other person's wishes with one's own; Kei agrees and identifies the relationship cost. body_claim_revisions.previous: [KEI-P015] The private002 episode makes embodiment ordinary as well as consequential. Kei acknowledges that body change worked, rejects the former body and expresses a qualified liking for cuteness. Her stiffness is metaphorical at this grade; the rejected WE-40 suggestion does not create a medical recommendation. A qualified report about an earlier body being picked up or apparently disposed of, together with gratitude, remains her account rather than a verified disposal or reconstruction record. Within these limits the scene still establishes present preference. She can value the body and want a particular aesthetic change without those desires having to prove the origin of the body or its stable performance in every setting. (KEI-S01 L87–91; KQ02, KQ04–05.)

body_claim_revisions.previous: [KEI-P023] The arcade invitation is not an observed visit. A previously enjoyed outing is reported and acknowledged, while the present response 悪くありません is more guarded than Sensei's translation into liking it. Her protest preserves that difference. This is another local form of positive company whose terms should remain visible: she can value an experience without choosing the adult's strongest paraphrase of her feeling. It is also a useful limit on chronology. A past report, a current invitation and an unperformed future visit are three distinct temporal acts; they should not be compressed into one completed outing or used as an attendance gate for how seriously her ordinary preferences count. (KEI-S01 L105–107; KQ02–03, KQ09–11.)

body_claim_revisions.previous: [KEI-P026] The strongest self-critical turn is the recognition that a critic may substitute their own wants for those of the makers. Kei's capacity to identify problems is therefore accompanied by a limit on the ownership of the project. Accepting Sensei's feedback proposal is an actual choice within the represented scene, not a renunciation of criticism or a guarantee that the resulting game succeeds. This matters for agency because she is not merely either an expert enforcing a correct design or a servant forbidden to object. The available compromise retains criticism, maker preference and another person's suggestion as distinct contributions to a shared work. It is a local ethical adjustment, with later delivery still unprinted. (KEI-S01 L111–117; KQ03–06, KQ11.)
body_claim_revisions.current: [KEI-P026] The strongest self-critical turn is the recognition that a critic may substitute their own wants for those of the makers. Kei's capacity to identify problems is therefore accompanied by a limit on the ownership of the project. Kei raises the difficulty of conveying feedback, agrees with the risk articulated in Sensei's written choice group, and explains that imposing on the makers would damage their relationship. This is recognition of a limit on her own criticism, not acceptance of a newly proposed feedback action or a guarantee that the resulting game succeeds. This matters for agency because she is not merely either an expert enforcing a correct design or a servant forbidden to object. The exchange retains criticism, maker preference and the teacher's understanding as distinct contributions to a shared work. It supports an interpretation of ethical self-restraint; a subsequent change in feedback practice or completed delivery is not shown. (KEI-S01 L111–117; KQ03–06, KQ11.)

body_claim_revisions.previous: [KEI-P027] The reported pleasure in everyone's happiness after completed work should not be applied prematurely to the current alpha. The narrative seam from enjoying herself toward diligent QA, together with gaps in the adult's memory and fatigue, keeps the work's cost visible. Pleasure in making can coexist with exhaustion; a comic transition does not prove that all labor has become healthy or freely chosen. The scene's finite positive is depicted work and a feedback route accepted under discussion. Its finite limits are bugs, ambitions, uneven labor and absent completion. This is sufficient for a substantial account of ordinary making, without a completed software model or a universal claim that the person now finds every service task fulfilling. (KEI-S01 L113–117; KQ02, KQ04–06, KQ11.)

body_claim_revisions.previous: [KEI-P053] Across the private material, care is offered, requested, criticized and sometimes appropriated. Kei asks for rescue, release and different praise; she also uses schedule access and summons against an objection. Sensei apologizes and thanks her over cleaning, proposes feedback and receives chosen company; he also teases, watches approvingly instead of releasing and disregards the gift return request in the event-local section. These directed acts cannot be reduced to a ledger of who is kind. They show that support can meet one need while overlooking another. Respect for agency requires particular responses to particular wishes, and the body cannot distribute a universal ethical certificate to either participant from a collection of warm endpoints. (KEI-S01 L93–133, L137; KEI-S02 L34–48; KQ03–06, KQ07.)

body_claim_revisions.previous: [KEI-P057] The represented longitudinal development is therefore a comparison of states and repertoires, not a recovered continuous life history. Main classification and coercive function, inward naming, an unauthenticated file, modern authored self-definition and ordinary participation provide meaningful successive interpretive contexts. Their full diegetic placement and mechanism remain unresolved. Within the private sequence there are more secure local developments: consideration followed by received invitations, a material task and gift received, criticism adjusting to maker preference, cleaning acknowledged and company chosen after a refused gesture. These finite changes support depth without substituting the later profile for earlier source knowledge or making one late positive scene a universal forecast. body_claim_revisions.previous: [KEI-P061] Rival04 is the perfectly sensitive mentor. Reassurance, proposed feedback, apology, thanks and chosen accompanied return give this view substantial local evidence. It fails against popularity teasing instead of rescue, approval instead of release, unwanted repetition of cuteness and the event recipient's continued eating after a return demand. The adverse cases do not invalidate every positive response; they show that a good intention or accepted company is not enough to certify responsiveness in every interaction. Kei's own pressure on the adult's schedule keeps the relation from becoming a one-directional moral caricature. Each initiative and response should retain its actor and direction, so that support and disregard can coexist without canceling one another. (KEI-S01 L95–133, L137; KEI-S02 L38–48; KQ03, KQ07, KQ10.)
